audit_scope.description: This batch predominantly covers EL logic: EVM interpreter, precompiled contracts (BLAKE2F, MODEXP), block processing, transaction lifecycle, fork activation, and P2P transaction propagation. EIP-7577 (versioning) is a meta/process EIP with no direct EL/CL runtime impact.

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EL component. The Transaction Executor is part of the EVM execution pipeline, not an external entity. It processes transactions within the EL.
Trace consumers (debuggers, monitoring tools) are downstream readers of trace output. They do not send data INTO the EVM; they only consume output. Not a threat source for the EL.

Internal EL component. A contract calling BLAKE2F is internal EVM execution (CALL opcode to precompile address 0x09). The ultimate source of data is the transaction submitter, not the calling contract itself.
Internal EL component. Same as EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER — a contract invoking MODEXP precompile is internal EVM execution.
Internal EL component. The 'calling contract providing input data' is within EVM execution context. The trust boundary is at transaction submission, not at internal precompile calls.
DApp event listeners are downstream consumers of provider events. They do not send data into the EL; they subscribe to events. Not a threat source.
EIP-7577 is a meta/process EIP about versioning governance. EIP authors interact with the EIPs repository, not with EL/CL runtime systems.
Same as EXT-EIP-AUTHOR — interacts with governance tooling, not EL/CL runtime.
Repository CI/CD tooling for EIP governance. Not an external entity interacting with EL/CL runtime.
Incoming Block is not an entity but a data object. The actual external entity is the network peer that sends the block.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. Transaction data (including calldata to precompiles like BLAKE2F, MODEXP), gas parameters, and timeout values are fully attacker-controlled. Covers EIP-7966 synchronous submission and EIP-2831 transaction replacement/speedup/cancel flows.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL sends withdrawal data (EXT-BEACON-CHAIN), block metadata, and parent_beacon_block_root via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated but payload content (withdrawal amounts, validator indices, beacon roots) must still be validated by the EL. Covers Cancun block withdrawal processing and beacon root validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/68 protocol (NewPooledTransactionHashes, GetPooledTransactions, block propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated and may be malicious. They send block headers for validation, transaction announcements with type/size metadata (EIP-5793 eth/68), and full transaction data. Peers can lie about transaction sizes, send invalid blocks, or attempt eclipse/amplification attacks. Covers EXT-NETWORK-PEER, EXT-PEER-NODES, EXT-ANNOUNCING-PEER, EXT-PEER, and EXT-ATTACKER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via Provider API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet Provider Interface (tx_speedup, tx_cancel, tx_replacement events)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet users initiate transaction replacement, speed-up, and cancellation through the provider interface (EIP-2831). While users control their own transactions, the provider must validate replacement invariants (nonce match, gas increase). A malicious or compromised wallet could emit false events.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, balance sufficiency, calldata bounds checking. For EIP-7966: timeout parameter must be validated (positive integer, not exceeding node maximum) to prevent resource exhaustion from long-held connections.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM Precompile dispatch (BLAKE2F at 0x09, MODEXP at 0x05)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Precompile input validation is critical. BLAKE2F: must verify exactly 213 bytes input and final flag is 0 or 1. MODEXP: must handle arbitrary-length inputs, zero-padding for short input, zero modulus edge case, and gas cost must accurately reflect computational complexity to prevent DoS. Attacker-controlled calldata flows through transaction submission to precompile execution.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API (withdrawal processing, beacon block root)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Channel is JWT-authenticated (SEMI_TRUSTED), but EL must validate withdrawal field types (U64 index, U64 validator_index, Address, U256 amount), verify withdrawals_root matches commitment, and validate parent_beacon_block_root. Malicious withdrawal data could create ETH from nothing or credit wrong addresses.

Full block header validation required: parent_hash, ommers_hash (must be EMPTY_OMMER_HASH), state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, excess_blob_gas (EIP-4844), and parent_beacon_block_root. Fork criteria must correctly select validation rules based on block number or timestamp. Peers are fully untrusted.

Peers can lie about transaction type and size in eth/68 announcements. Node must: validate array length consistency (types, sizes, hashes must have equal length), apply bandwidth throttling based on announced sizes, track per-peer behavior for reputation scoring, and validate actual transaction data after fetching. Size metadata is advisory only — actual fetched transactions may differ.

Provider must validate replacement invariants: for speed-up, same nonce/recipient/value/data with >=10% gas increase; for cancel, same nonce with self-send (from==to, value=0, empty data); for generic replacement, only nonce match required. Must verify original transaction is still pending (not yet mined).
